subject: general
question: The price of commodity X increases by 40 paise every year, while the price of commodity Y increases by 25 paise every year. If, in the year 2002, the price of X was Rs. 5.20 and that of Y was Rs. 6.30, then in which year would commodity X cost 40 paise more than commodity Y?
solution:
**Given:**

Price of X in 2002 = ₹5.20

Price of Y in 2002 = ₹6.30

Price increase of X per year = 40 paise = ₹0.40

Price increase of Y per year = 25 paise = ₹0.25

**Formula used:**

Price of X in year n = Price of X in 2002 + (n - 2002) × 0.40

Price of Y in year n = Price of Y in 2002 + (n - 2002) × 0.25

**Calculation:**

We need to find the year when the price of X is 40 paise more than the price of Y:

Price of X in year n = Price of Y in year n + 0.40

⇒ 5.20 + (n - 2002) × 0.40 = 6.30 + (n - 2002) × 0.25 + 0.40

⇒ 5.20 + 0.40n - 0.40 × 2002 = 6.30 + 0.25n - 0.25 × 2002 + 0.40

⇒ 5.20 + 0.40n - 800.8 = 6.30 + 0.25n - 500.5 + 0.40

⇒ 5.20 + 0.40n - 800.8 = 6.70 + 0.25n - 500.5

⇒ 0.40n - 0.25n = 6.70 - 5.20 - 500.5 + 800.8

⇒ 0.15n = 1.50 + 300.3

⇒ 0.15n = 301.8

⇒ n = 301.8 / 0.15

⇒ n = 2012

**∴ The correct answer is option 1 (2012).**
